open_account.title: Open account
open_account.description: Return the account for this (category, holder_id), opening it if it does not exist yet. Opening is lazy and idempotent: an account exists because something was posted to it, never because its holder merely registered, and asking twice returns the same account rather than a second one.

get_account.title: Read account
get_account.description: Read one account by its storage id.

args.description: The account to read.

list_accounts.title: List accounts
list_accounts.description: List the chart of accounts, oldest-opened first.

args.description: Cap the accounts returned. Zero or absent means the default page.

close_account.title: Close account
close_account.description: Stamp an account closed. Refused while it still carries a balance, and refused if it is already closed.

args.description: The account to close.

account_balance.title: Read balance
account_balance.description: Fold one account's balance: everything debited to it minus everything credited from it, over every entry naming it. There is no stored balance anywhere in this module, so this is computed on every call.

args.description: The account to fold.

post_entry.title: Post entry
post_entry.description: Append one journal entry, debiting one account and crediting another for the same amount. There is no update and no delete: a mistake is corrected by posting a new entry that names the original in reverses_entry_id, and an entry may be reversed at most once. A reversal keeps its original's dimensions. A payment may name the charge it pays in settles_entry_id, which must be an entry already in the ledger.

list_entries.title: List entries
list_entries.description: Read one account's ledger, both sides, ordered on when the event occurred and falling back to when it was posted, oldest first so a running balance can be accumulated down the page.

args.description: The account whose ledger to read.
Cap the entries returned. Zero or absent means the default page.

set_budget.title: Set budget
set_budget.description: Set one budget line: what one account is expected to hold over one period, with a name and the department it belongs to. Setting it again for the same account and period replaces the name, department, amount, follow_milestones and cost_shares, so send them back unchanged to keep them; follow_milestones true makes a reader show the line's milestones and payment certificates, and cost_shares, a neighbourhood name to a whole percent that add up to 100, spreads the line's spending over those neighbourhoods in the totals by neighbourhood, where absent each spending entry stays with the neighbourhood it names; send version, the set_at you read, to be refused when the line has changed since; send create true when adding a new line, to be refused when that account and period already hold one. The period runs from period_start, inclusive, to period_end, exclusive.

variance.title: Read variance
variance.description: Read one account's budget for a period beside its actual balance over that period, and the difference, actual minus budgeted. The actual folds only entries whose occurred_at, or posted_at where that is absent, falls inside the period.

args.description: The account to compare.
The period's first instant, inclusive, exactly as the budget was set.
The period's end, exclusive, exactly as the budget was set.

add_milestone.title: Add milestone
add_milestone.description: Record one stage of a contract against the account its spending is booked to, with what it is worth and when it is planned to be reached. It starts planned and is paid only through payment certificates.

list_milestones.title: List milestones
list_milestones.description: List the milestones planned against one account, oldest first, each with the amount certified so far.

args.description: The account whose milestones to list.
Cap the milestones returned. Zero or absent means the default page.

certify_payment.title: Certify payment
certify_payment.description: Issue a payment certificate for all or part of a milestone. The amount less the retention is posted from the milestone's account to the payee, and the retention, a share of the amount in hundredths of a percent, is posted to the retention account until it is released. Refused when the certificates would add up to more than the milestone is worth.

args.description: The milestone certified. The address decides, not the body.
Who certified the work, supplied by the mount. Never read from the request.

list_certificates.title: List certificates
list_certificates.description: List the payment certificates issued for one milestone, oldest first, each with its retention and whether it has been released.

args.description: The milestone whose certificates to list.
Cap the certificates returned. Zero or absent means the default page.

release_retention.title: Release retention
release_retention.description: Pay out the retention a certificate withheld, from the retention account to the payee. Refused before the certificate's release date, when nothing was withheld, and when it was already released.

args.description: The certificate whose retention to release.
Who released the retention, supplied by the mount. Never read from the request.

overdue_entries.title: List overdue entries
overdue_entries.description: Read one account's entries whose due_at has passed as of an instant, each with the whole days it is overdue, oldest first by age_days, which is the same as days_overdue unless age_from is "raised". An entry with no due_at is never listed, nor is an entry that has been reversed or one that reverses another. Unreversed entries naming a charge in settles_entry_id are netted against it: each item carries what is still outstanding, and a charge paid in full is not listed.

args.description: The account whose overdue entries to read.
The instant to age against, as an RFC 3339 instant. Absent means now.

Where each item's age_days starts counting and what the list is ordered on: "due" (the default) from the entry's due_at, "raised" from the day the entry was posted. Which entries are listed does not change. Any other value is refused.

list_entries_by_dimension.title: List entries by dimension
list_entries_by_dimension.description: Read one account's ledger narrowed to the entries whose dimensions carry the named key with exactly the given value, in the same order as the full listing.

args.description: The account whose ledger to read.
The dimension key to narrow by.
The value that key must carry.
Cap the entries returned. Zero or absent means the default page.

dimension_balance.title: Read balance by dimension
dimension_balance.description: Fold one account's debits minus credits over only the entries whose dimensions carry the named key with exactly the given value. The balances of an account under every value of one key sum to its whole balance only when every entry carries that key.

args.description: The account whose balance to read.
The dimension key to narrow by.
The value that key must carry.

append_figure.title: Append figure
append_figure.description: Append one entry to the record of figures: a figure that is not money, kept for one subject on one day with how it was worked out (the function code, the published version and a fingerprint of the inputs) and who caused it. The record sits beside the ledger and holds no money. There is no update and no delete, and a second entry for the same subject, figure and day is refused. The value is decimal text and keeps its digits as written.

list_figure_history.title: List a figure's history
list_figure_history.description: Read the history of one figure of one subject, newest day first, each entry with its provenance.

args.description: The subject the figure is kept for.
The name of the figure.
Cap the entries returned. Zero or absent means the default page.

dimension_totals.title: Read totals by dimension
dimension_totals.description: Fold debit minus credit per value of one dimension key, over the entry sides that fall on accounts of the given type, or on every account when no type is given, in which case each entry nets to zero. Entries that do not carry the key are skipped, except that for the key neighbourhood the spending on an account whose budget line shares its cost is split over the line's neighbourhoods by their percents, whatever neighbourhood the entry names, with any remainder of a division going to the largest share. The period is optional; when given both bounds are required, and only entries whose occurred_at, or posted_at where that is absent, falls inside it count, start inclusive and end exclusive. Totals come sorted by value.

args.description: The dimension key to total by.
Only count entry sides on accounts of this type. Absent means every account.
The period's first instant, inclusive. Required with period_end.
The period's end, exclusive. Required with period_start.

delete_budget_line.title: Delete budget line
delete_budget_line.description: Delete one budget line that nothing has been spent on: it is refused with 409 when any entry of its account falls inside its period, or when a tender draws on it. Send version, the set_at you read, to be refused when the line has changed since. Returns the line that was removed.

args.description: The budget line to delete.
The set_at of the line as you read it; the delete is refused when the line has changed since. Absent means no check.

add_day_allowance.title: Add day allowance
add_day_allowance.description: Record the days bought for one consultant on one project: the days in hundredths of a day, the fee for a day, and an optional period. A consultant has one current allowance on a project; a change goes through replace_day_allowance, never a second row. Refused when the consultant already holds one, whatever the case or spacing of the name, and when days times rate would not fit a whole number.

args.description: Who set the allowance, supplied by the mount. Never read from the request.

replace_day_allowance.title: Replace day allowance
replace_day_allowance.description: Change the days bought by writing a new row that names the current row it replaces and says why. The old row stays as history. The replaced row must be the consultant's current one on the same project, and a reason is required. Refused with 409 when the new days are fewer than the consultant's approved days, and refused when days times rate would not fit a whole number. A new rate prices days approved from then on; days already approved keep the rate they were approved at.

args.description: The allowance row replaced. The address decides, not the body.
Who changed the allowance, supplied by the mount. Never read from the request.

list_day_allowances.title: List day allowances
list_day_allowances.description: Read every allowance row of one project, the replaced ones included, oldest first.

args.description: The project.
Cap the rows returned. Zero or absent means the default page.

submit_day_entry.title: Submit day entry
submit_day_entry.description: Record days worked by one consultant on one project on one date, in hundredths of a day. It starts submitted and counts toward nothing until it is approved. A day is at most 100 hundredths, and one consultant's submitted and approved entries on one date add up to at most that; refused with 409 when the date would hold more.

args.description: Who submitted the entry, supplied by the mount. Never read from the request.

approve_day_entry.title: Approve day entry
approve_day_entry.description: Approve a submitted entry. Refused with 409 when the consultant's approved days would pass the days bought on the project, or when the consultant holds no allowance there, until a replacing allowance row raises the days. Refused when the entry was already decided, and refused with 409 when the person approving is the one who submitted the entry or the consultant it names. The entry is stamped with the day rate of the allowance in force at approval.

args.description: The entry to approve.
Who approved the entry, supplied by the mount. Never read from the request.

reject_day_entry.title: Reject day entry
reject_day_entry.description: Reject a submitted entry. A rejected entry counts toward nothing. Refused when the entry was already decided.

args.description: The entry to reject.
Who rejected the entry, supplied by the mount. Never read from the request.

list_day_entries.title: List day entries
list_day_entries.description: Read the day entries of one project, oldest worked date first, narrowed by consultant and by status when given.

args.description: The project.
Only this consultant's entries.
Only entries with this status: submitted, approved or rejected.
Cap the entries returned. Zero or absent means the default page.

days_balance.title: Read days balance
days_balance.description: For one project, per consultant and position: the days bought, the days submitted and still awaiting a decision, the days approved, the days left, the fee approved days come to, each at the rate it was approved at, the fee left (the days left at the current rate), and the fee ceiling, which is the fee plus the fee left. A total line sums them. Days are hundredths of a day. Only the current allowance row of each consultant counts.

args.description: The project.

list_budget_lines.title: List budget lines
list_budget_lines.description: List budget lines, each with its name, department, period, planned amount and what was spent in that period so far. Spent is the account's balance over the period, debits minus credits, folded on every call. Narrow by account_id or department; limit caps the page.

get_budget_line.title: Read budget line
get_budget_line.description: Read one budget line by its id, with its planned amount and what was spent in its period so far.

args.description: The budget line to read.

list_reports.title: List financial reports
list_reports.description: List financial reports, one for each period that has budget lines, oldest period first. Each has a name, the period, its figures and its budget lines. The figures are the planned and spent totals and their difference, planned minus spent, the same split by department, and the closing balance of each account type at the period end, all folded on every call. Limit caps the page.

get_report.title: Read financial report
get_report.description: Read the financial report of one period: its name, figures and budget lines. The difference is planned minus spent. The period is named exactly as its budget lines were set.

args.description: The period's first instant, inclusive, exactly as the budget lines were set.
The period's end, exclusive, exactly as the budget lines were set.

send_upward_report.title: Send upward report
send_upward_report.description: Record that the report of one period was sent upward. The report is folded at that moment, the same one accounting_report_read gives, and one record is kept: its kind, the period, the planned, spent and difference totals as sent (the difference is planned minus spent), the department figures, when it was sent and who sent it. Kind is budget_and_actuals, which also keeps every budget line, or spending_by_department, which keeps the department figures only. Name who it went to if known: recipient (the name as written), recipient_record_row_id (the recipient's row in a record, a uuid; reports can then be listed by recipient_record_row_id) and reference (the recipient's own contract or grant number); all three are optional and kept as sent, never edited. Name project to cut the report for one project: only the budget lines whose department is that project are folded, and each line's spent counts only entries carrying the dimension project with that value; the project is kept as sent. Without project the whole period is folded as before. Refused for any other kind, for a recipient_record_row_id that is not a uuid, for a project that is not a valid dimension value, and for a period with no budget lines (for a project: with no budget line of that project). A second send of the same period and kind is another record, never an edit. Nothing is transmitted over a network.

args.description: Who sent the report, supplied by the mount. Never read from the request.

list_upward_reports.title: List upward reports
list_upward_reports.description: List the reports sent upward, newest first, each with its kind, period, the planned, spent and difference totals as sent (the difference is planned minus spent), the department figures, the budget lines when the kind keeps them, when it was sent, who sent it and, when it named them, its recipient, recipient_record_row_id and reference. Narrow by recipient_record_row_id to list the reports sent to one recipient, by project to list the reports cut for one project, or by both; limit caps the page.

create_tender.title: Create tender
create_tender.description: Open a tender: what is to be bought and the budget line it draws on, with the date quotes close if there is one. Refused when the budget line does not exist.

args.description: Who opened the tender, supplied by the mount. Never read from the request.

list_tenders.title: List tenders
list_tenders.description: List tenders, oldest first, each with how many quotes it has and the lowest amount quoted. Narrow by budget_id; limit caps the page.

get_tender.title: Read tender
get_tender.description: Read one tender by its id, with how many quotes it has and the lowest amount quoted.

args.description: The tender to read.

create_quote.title: Record quote
create_quote.description: Record one supplier's offer for a tender: who offers, the price in the smallest unit and what it includes. A supplier that changes its offer is recorded again as a new quote.

args.description: The tender the quote answers. The address decides, not the body.
Who recorded the quote, supplied by the mount. Never read from the request.

update_bill.title: Correct bill
update_bill.description: Correct a bill that is not yet settled: send its payer, payer_actor_id (the payer's person id), payer_record_row_id (the payer's business or trader record row id), amount, due_at and narration as they should now read; project (the project key the bill is raised for) as it should now read; a correction that leaves payer_actor_id, payer_record_row_id or project out clears that link. A bill that already has a payment keeps its amount, and a settled or reversed bill is refused.

args.description: The bill to correct.

update_tender.title: Correct tender
update_tender.description: Correct a tender before its closing date: send its title, description and closes_at as they should now read. The budget line it draws on stays as recorded. Refused once the tender has closed.

args.description: The tender to correct.

update_quote.title: Correct quote
update_quote.description: Correct one supplier's quote before its tender closes: send the supplier, the price in the smallest unit, the note and valid_until as they should now read. Refused once the tender has closed.

args.description: The quote to correct.

list_quotes.title: List quotes
list_quotes.description: List the quotes offered for one tender, lowest price first.

args.description: The tender whose quotes to list.
Cap the quotes returned. Zero or absent means the default page.

create_bill.title: Create bill
create_bill.description: Raise a bill: an amount owed to an income account, due on a date. It is posted as a debit to the receivable account and a credit to the income account, with due_at set, so the overdue read ages it. Name the income account, the receivable account (an asset account), the amount, due_at and, if known, the payer (display text) payer_actor_id (the payer's person id, a uuid; bills can then be listed by actor_id) and payer_record_row_id (the payer's business or informal trader record row id, a uuid; bills can then be listed by record_row_id). Name the project it is raised for in project (a short text, the same project key the fee entries carry, at most 200 characters; bills can then be listed by project and totalled with dimension totals of key project and account_type asset). A payment settles a bill by naming it in settles_entry_id.

args.description: Who raised the bill, supplied by the mount. Never read from the request.

list_bills.title: List bills
list_bills.description: List bills by due date, each with its amount, what was settled, what is outstanding and its status: open, overdue (past due_at as of as_of, default now, and not fully settled), settled or reversed. Narrow by income_account_id, status, payer (the name as written) actor_id (the payer's person id, set as payer_actor_id when the bill was raised) or record_row_id (a business or trader record row id, set as payer_record_row_id when the bill was raised; bills raised against an older row it replaced are listed too) or project (set as project when the bill was raised); limit caps the page.

get_bill.title: Read bill
get_bill.description: Read one bill by its id, with what was settled against it, what is outstanding and its status as of now.

args.description: The bill to read.

mark_bill_paid.title: Mark bill paid
mark_bill_paid.description: Record that a bill was paid: posts a debit to the cash account (an asset account) and a credit to the bill's receivable account, naming the bill in settles_entry_id, so the bill reads as settled. The payment carries the bill's payer, payer_actor_id and payer_record_row_id. Leave amount out to pay what is outstanding; a smaller amount is a part payment. Refused when the bill is already settled or reversed, or the amount is more than is outstanding. paid_on is when the money arrived, if not now, and is refused when it is in the future; method (how it was paid, such as cash or bank transfer) and reference are kept with the payment and listed back.

args.description: The bill paid. The address decides, not the body.
Who recorded the payment, supplied by the mount. Never read from the request.

reverse_payment.title: Reverse payment
reverse_payment.description: Reverse one payment of a bill that was recorded by mistake or in the wrong amount: a new line is posted that undoes it and names it in reverses_entry_id, so the bill owes what it owed before and the payment is left out of the list of payments. The original stays in the ledger, nothing is deleted. A payment is reversed once, only a payment of a bill can be reversed, and the line records who reversed it and the narration, if one is given.

args.description: The payment reversed. The address decides, not the body.
Who reversed the payment, supplied by the mount. Never read from the request.

list_payments.title: List payments
list_payments.description: List payments, oldest first: the payments that settled bills (kind bill, each naming its bill_id) and the milestone payment certificates (kind certificate, each naming its certificate, milestone and contract, the amount being what was paid after retention). A reversed payment is left out. Narrow by kind, bill_id, payer (the name as written) actor_id (the payer's person id) or record_row_id (a business or trader record row id; bills against an older row it replaced are listed too); certificate payments carry none of these and are left out when one is named; limit caps the page.

dimension_entries.title: List the entries of one dimension value
dimension_entries.description: Every entry whose dimensions carry the given key with exactly the given value, across all accounts, each with the day it happened (occurred_at, or posted_at where that is absent), its amount on the entry sides that fall on accounts of the given type (debit minus credit; every account when no type is given), its narration and the category of the account it fell on, newest first. The period is optional; when given both bounds are required, start inclusive and end exclusive.

args.description: The dimension key to read by.
The value that key must carry.
Only count entry sides on accounts of this type. Absent means every account.
The period's first instant, inclusive. Required with period_end.
The period's end, exclusive. Required with period_start.

create_rate.title: Enter exchange rate
create_rate.description: Enter one exchange rate: how many units of the counter currency one unit of the base currency buys on a date, as a whole number scaled by 100000000 (140.00 KES per EUR is base EUR, counter KES, rate 14000000000). Kind is daily, monthly (applies to the whole month of applies_on) or agreed. Name the source the rate comes from. A rate is never edited: a correction is a new row with replaces_id naming the one it corrects, same pair, kind and date. A pair is held in one direction only; a rate in the other direction is refused. Refused for an unknown currency code, equal currencies, a rate that is not positive and a date that is not 2006-01-02.

args.description: Who entered the rate, supplied by the mount. Never read from the request.

list_rates.title: List exchange rates
list_rates.description: List the exchange rates in force, oldest entered first. A rate that a later row corrected is left out. Narrow by base, counter or kind; limit caps the page.

get_converted_report.title: Read financial report in one currency
get_converted_report.description: Read the financial report of one period with every amount converted into reporting_currency by one rule: posting_date (the daily rate on the day each entry happened), posting_month (the monthly rate of the month each entry happened in), period_average (the mean of the daily rates inside the period, applied to the period's total in each currency) or report_date (the rate on the last day of the period, applied to each currency's total). Each line shows its budget and spending converted, and beside them the amounts as entered, one for each currency. The report names the rule and prints every rate it used with its source. A rate that does not exist is never guessed: the figure is left out, the report says complete false and lists the missing pair and date. A bill paid in a currency whose rate moved between billing and payment shows an exchange difference as its own line, in the reporting currency, and not inside the spending. Rounding is once, to the smallest unit of the reporting currency: per entry for the two posting rules, per currency total for the other two.

account_balances_by_currency.title: Read balance in each currency
account_balances_by_currency.description: Fold one account's balance once for each currency it holds entries in, debits minus credits, never adding two currencies together. A plain balance read is refused when the account holds more than one currency.

args.description: The account to fold.
